clue.text: Conservative going to bar in place in 12

explanation.surface: A Tory politician heads for the pub in a Scottish town.

explanation.definitionFit: Crail is a small harbour town on the East Neuk coast of the Scottish county.

clue.text: Party carrying end of wicker hamper

explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a picnic basket, matching 'wicker', but it is a verb meaning hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to restrict or hinder, as a muscle spasm or confined space does.

clue.text: Key period almost squandered, offering chance to change

explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter off BLEW to leave BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be modified is open to change, so it offers that possibility.

clue.text: Story about doctor and us in a big car

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the others

MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious chauffeur-driven motor.

clue.text: Many tips distributed by tense performer on 19

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread about into a new order

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

clue.text: Emperor fit to return around Troy

parts.note: to suit is to fit, be right for

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor ready to come back to the walls of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts T inside SUIT reversed (TIUS). 'Troy' looks like the city, but it stands for troy weight.

clue.text: Description of some brides, look, captured by 'married', possibly

indicators.note: captured by means the first piece is held inside the second
possibly signals that the letters may be rearranged

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold

explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' is the anagram signal on 'married', and 'captured by' puts the old word for look inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail-order bride is a woman who meets her husband through a catalogue or agency.

clue.text: Something emanating from the ears, needing to be curtailed

parts.note: aural means relating to the ears or hearing

explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a subtle glow or atmosphere seen as radiating from a person or thing.

clue.text: Independent in City picking up tribal following

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were the British tribe led by Boudicca against Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British people of East Anglia, a tribe and its members.

clue.text: We like working in test roughly every other day

explanation.walkthrough: 'working' is the anagram signal, and 'in' sets the result inside the word for test.

clue.text: US lawyer bringing in contract staff member for trial

indicators.note: bringing in means the first piece holds the second inside

explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' tempts as a court case, matching 'lawyer', but it means a try.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial or attempt is an effort to do something, a go at it.

clue.text: Attention's recalled, captured by heart of smiling Middle East resident

heart of keeps the middle letters of the word smiling

explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses the word, 'heart of' keeps the inner three letters of smiling, and 'captured by' puts one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Israel lives in the Middle East.

clue.text: Runs copies off for 19s

explanation.walkthrough: 19 is DRUM; 'Runs copies off' reads as printing, but 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Drums are the core of the struck-instrument section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Instrument provided, cast in iron

clue.text: Surrendered marine vessel: sea claims it with time

indicators.note: claims means takes in, holding the other letters

clue.text: Place in 12 also featuring in spreads

indicators.note: featuring in means the word is set inside the other one

parts.note: strews means scatters, spreads about
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A Scottish town also appearing in newspaper spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is FIFE; the town is the home of golf and its ancient university.
explanation.definitionFit: The golfing town lies on the coast of the Scottish county of Fife.

clue.text: A lot of pages supplied after money received? Have a holiday

indicators.note: supplied after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: the take is the takings, money received

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: leaves are the pages of a book

explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off work, so taking it means going away on a break.

clue.text: Czech playwright placing Knight on headland

K is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.definitionFit: Karel Čapek wrote R.U.R., the play that gave the world the word robot.

clue.text: Operations in repeated patterns will do for monsters

indicators.note: in means the short word sits inside the longer one

parts.note: cycles are patterns that repeat

clue.text: Stolid and hardly excited about energy forms

clue.text: A suggestion of cancellation from British singer

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to delete something

clue.text: Starship captain caught with alien lady in place in 12

clue.text: Briefly had booze in barrel

clue.text: Can we appear obsessed hackers ultimately?

definitions.text: Can we appear obsessed hackers ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of each word is taken

clue.text: Woman at the outset is picking up kitchen accessory
